text:
[LSIG.2.5.1] Eviction of backing state is driven by new assertions, not by
query time, but every query returns a fresh answer as of the monotonic clock's
sample `t` ([LTIM.2.8.2]): the
query walks and discounts the not-yet-evicted out-of-window portion without
mutating stored state. `active_fraction`, `onset_rate`, and `integral`
therefore all evaluate as of the same instant `t` and may be combined in one
rule without a freshness mismatch. Worst-case query cost is O(K), bounded by
the declared `.dsrt` capacity under `realtime` (§[LSIG.5]).

idris.name: Lsig_2_5_1__store
idris.note: THE STORE: the monotonic samples at which a series' values were absorbed and not yet evicted. What a value is is not modelled; which values take part in a query is.

idris.name: lsig_2_5_1__discount
idris.note: THE DISCOUNT: what a query at a sample sees of the store for a window -- the members still in the window at that sample, the rest discounted, the store not mutated. 'The query walks and discounts the not-yet-evicted out-of-window portion without mutating stored state', reduced to membership.

idris.name: lsig_2_5_1__discount_after_eviction
idris.note: EVICTION IS DRIVEN BY ASSERTIONS, NOT BY QUERY TIME, AND THE QUERY'S ANSWER IS THE SAME: for every store, every window, every monotonic sample of an eviction and every later sample of a query, and whatever the wall clock read at either, the discount at the query of the store evicted at the assertion is the discount at the query of the store. Eviction may lag a query by any number of samples or run at every one. By induction on the store, from `lsig_2_5_1__out_stays_out`.

idris.name: lsig_2_5_1__evict
idris.note: EVICTION, at the sample of a new assertion: the store keeps what is in the window at that sample. The same filter as the discount, applied to the store and kept; the clause's claim is that applying it early changes nothing a later discount sees, which is the theorem below.

idris.name: lsig_2_5_1__eviction_not_at_query_time
idris.note: EXECUTED: values absorbed at 1, 2 and 3, a window of 2; an eviction at sample 3 drops the value of 1; a query at sample 4 sees the value of 3 alone, evicted or not.

idris.name: lsig_2_5_1__not_both
idris.note: A Boolean is not both `True` and `False`. A helper.

idris.name: lsig_2_5_1__out_stays_out
idris.note: OUT STAYS OUT: a value out of the window at one monotonic sample is out at every later one, whatever the wall clock reads at either. The `in_window` instance of Rete/EntryStamp.idr's `ltim_2_7_1__within_falls`: membership is `within`'s formula, and `within` falls once on a clock that does not go back.

idris.name: lsig_2_5_1__query_before_eviction_differs
idris.note: THE HYPOTHESIS IS NEEDED: an eviction at a sample after the query's drops a value the query would have seen. The theorem asks the eviction's sample to be at or before the query's, which [LTIM.2.8.2]'s clock gives between an assertion and a later query; a store evicted in the query's future is not the clause's case.
